cover: The cover of GPU Architecture & Parallel Programming from First Principles. Inside a glowing hive, the queen bee, wearing a crown and holding a sceptre, gives one order to the whole colony: c[i] = a[i] + b[i]. Below her, 32 worker bees in hard hats stand in 4 rows of 8, one warp, each in front of its own honeycomb cell and each filling it with honey at the same moment. One worker in the third row has wandered off on a branch of its own, with a question mark over its head. A crab in a hard hat waves from the corner, because the second half of the book writes kernels in Rust.
ch01: Tally, an ant, leads a column of ants carrying crumbs across a meadow. The column is wide where the ground is open, and every ant walks at once. Then it narrows to a single twig bridge over a stream, where only one ant can cross at a time and the rest wait in a queue. The bridge is the serial part of the work.
ch02: Comb, a worker bee in a hard hat, stands beside a hive with its side cut away. Inside hang three wooden comb frames, labelled SM 0, SM 1 and SM 2. On each frame small worker bees stand in straight rows that move together, a formation called a warp. Comb points at the frames like a guide on a tour.
ch03: The Queen bee, in her crown and sash, holds up a scroll that reads <<<4, 256>>>: a launch of 4 blocks of 256 threads. Beside her a wooden board holds 4 comb frames, labelled block 0 to block 3, and on each frame rows of worker bees wait for the order. The Queen gives one order and every bee on every frame carries it out.
ch04: Ferry, a pelican, stands on a wooden raft in the middle of a river, its beak pouch full of crates of bytes. On the left bank crates are stacked under a sign that reads host memory; on the right bank a sign reads device memory. A tag says pinned: 1 trip, because pinned data crosses in a single copy.
ch05: Whistle, a meerkat with a whistle, stands on watch beside a striped gate across a path. 3 worker bees have reached the gate and wait in a row; a 4th is still flying in from the left. The gate stays down until every bee has arrived. A sign on the gate reads __syncthreads(), and a tag says all arrive, then all go.
ch06: The otter twins float on their backs down 2 rivers that run side by side, each with a crate on its belly. Crates bob along both rivers at staggered places, so both streams carry work at the same time. Signs on the bank read stream 0 and stream 1, and a tag says 2 streams, at the same time.
ch13: Pinch, a crab in a hard hat, stands at a long table of numbered cells. Each claw picks up one input, a[i] in one and b[i] in the other, and the sum goes into the row c below. At the end of the row two small crabs have no cell to fill: they are the spare threads of the last block, and they doze.
